Question: Two \(600\) mL pitchers contain orange juice. One pitcher is \(\frac 13\) full and the other pitcher is \(\frac 25\) full. Water is added to fill each pitcher completely, then both pitchers are poured into one large container. What fraction of the mixture in the large container is orange juice?
Solution:
Adding water leaves the amount of orange juice unchanged, so first find how much juice the pitchers contain. Their juice volumes are
\[
600\cdot\frac13=200\text{ mL}
\quad\text{and}\quad
600\cdot\frac25=240\text{ mL}.
\]
After both pitchers are filled completely, their combined volume is \(600+600=1200\) mL. Of this, \(200+240=440\) mL is orange juice. Therefore the fraction that is orange juice is
\[
\frac{440}{1200}=\frac{11}{30}.
\]
The answer is \(\frac{11}{30}\), choice C.
